Subject: USW: Elevated latency due to GPU saturation — Statuspage advisory

Hi Jamie,

Quick heads-up from Redwood operations: we observed elevated p95/p99 latency for hosted text-generation endpoints in our US-West (usw1) region beginning around 08:40 PT this morning. Root cause is a transient GPU saturation condition on a subset of our inference pools after an unusual spike of long-context jobs. We opened an ops bridge at 08:55 and initiated autoscale and routing changes.

What this means for OmniHealth: you may have seen longer response times for large context requests (templates > 4k tokens). We did not see any data-plane errors or dropped requests; most requests were delayed by an extra 200-800ms while rerouting.

Actions taken so far:
- Diverted new traffic away from saturated pools and scaled additional reserved capacity in us-west.
- Applied temporary routing policy to favor lower-concurrency replicas for long-context jobs.
- Enabled additional KV-prefix cache to reduce repeated prefix compute for large prompts.

We have posted a condensed advisory on our status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/USW-0301 (live updates). Aditya is compiling a short diagnostics bundle which I’ve attached.

Next steps I’m proposing:
1) Keep the temporary routing policy in place for the next 4 hours while we validate new capacity.
2) We’ll follow up with a full postmortem and recommended guards (prompt-length guardrails, batching suggestions, and quota knobs) within 48 hours.

If you want a quick sync with our SREs I can loop in calendar availability. Sorry for the disruption — taking this seriously and will follow up with concrete mitigations.

Connor O’Brien

Hi Jamie, Connor,

Quick technical summary from the SRE team:
- Error surface: we did not observe an increase in 5xx responses for OmniHealth. All requests were served; p95 and p99 increased.
- Cause: a concentration of long-context synchronous jobs (several > 8k tokens) triggered sustained attention kernel load on a set of A100 pools. That produced local GPU queueing until we diverted traffic.
- Cost impact: temporary routing to lower-concurrency replicas increased per-request billing by ~3-6% for affected requests due to less efficient batching.
- Mitigation applied: scaling up more instances and immediate KV-prefix warm cache reduced the tail; by 10:30 PT we saw p95 recover to baseline and p99 improve steadily.

We’re also recommending the following for OmniHealth (short-term):
- If you have predictable long-context batch workloads, mark them as background/low-priority to route to dedicated capacity in Redwood Dedicated.
- Apply a soft prompt-length threshold on hosted traffic (we can help instrument an alert at 6k tokens).

Attaching a small excerpt of routing logs for transparency (incumbent-routing-logs-0301.txt). We’ll include a full postmortem in 48 hours with timeline, root cause analysis, and code-level mitigations.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
